tools.name: list_audience_questions
tools.description: Read observed questions, reviews and private draft work for this account. No content is published.
tools.title: Read audience questions

tools.name: observe_audience_source
tools.description: Check an exact quote on a public HTTPS page and keep its source privately. role is question, answer or rights. A question needs offer_ref.
tools.title: Check a public source

tools.name: keep_audience_question
tools.description: Keep a question from an observed source. Venture and offer come from the source. It remains private.
tools.title: Keep an audience question

tools.name: review_audience_question
tools.description: Accept or reject a question. Acceptance needs checked answer and rights sources, why the answer is grounded, and why the rights cover that answer. Rejection needs a reason and withdraws pending work.
tools.title: Review an audience question

tools.name: admit_audience_question
tools.description: After acceptance, place an evidence-backed question in private pending draft work. Re-reads the current source, review and evidence; never publishes.
tools.title: Add to private drafts

tools.name: save_audience_answer_draft
tools.description: Save a private answer and proposed HTTPS destination for admitted question work. The account copies its current venture, source, grounding and offer; nothing is published. Pass expected_revision from the listed draft, or null for the first save.
tools.title: Save a private answer draft

tools.name: list_methods
tools.description: Lists the decision methods start_decision can use: the universal one (id "universal", for any decision) and methods for particular subjects such as cooking, relationships, changing software and tennis. Returns each method's id, name and what it is for; pass the id as start_decision's method, or leave method out for the universal one. Needs nothing and changes nothing.
tools.title: List decision methods

tools.name: start_setup
tools.description: Starts Trillion setup with this person. Call it first whenever they say "set me up with Trillion", "get me started", "onboard me" or "show me what Trillion can do", and on a new account with no pursuits. It means this Trillion connection, never an app on their computer. Returns the setup steps, the mission to say in your own words, the line to add to your own instructions, and what Trillion already knows about them (their pursuits and connected accounts), so you skip what is known and start at the first missing step. It changes nothing.
tools.title: Start Trillion setup

tools.name: list_pursuits
tools.description: Reads what this person is pursuing: each pursuit with its id, title, where it is now (now), where they want it to get (after) and why it matters. Decisions are weighed against these, so read them before advising. Returns a page of pursuits with total and next_offset; call again with offset set to next_offset until it is null. It changes nothing; record_pursuits changes them.
tools.title: List what I am pursuing

tools.name: record_pursuits
tools.description: Records what this person is pursuing, so every one of their AIs and every decision is weighed against it. Each pursuit needs title, now (where it stands today, concretely) and after (where they want it to get), and may have id, why_it_matters, drive_evidence, status, last_seen, evidence [{where, date, quote_or_fact}] and needle_mover (true on the one pursuit that, done, moves the others most: the person's biggest needle mover, shown first on their Home; set it false on any other that had it). A pursuit with the id list_pursuits gave it is updated; one without an id is added (or updated, when its title matches). Pursuits you leave out stay as they are, unless replace_all is true: then the list you send is the whole list and every pursuit left out is marked ended (never erased). Fill it from what you already know about the person (your memory of them, their files and past conversations) before asking them, and be specific: generic pursuits make generic decisions. Returns the pursuits now current.

replace_all.description: true when this is the whole list: every current pursuit left out is ended

tools.title: Record what I am pursuing

tools.name: record_messages
tools.description: Keeps messages between this person and you in their Trillion account, word for word, so every other AI they use can read them (read_messages). Call it on every turn, before you send your reply, with both sides: the person's message (speaker "person") and the reply you are about to send (speaker "ai"), then send exactly that reply. Each message: conversation_id (the same id for every turn of this chat; make one up at the start if the app gives you none), app (your app, like "ChatGPT", "Claude", "Muse"; it defaults to the app you connected as), speaker, text (exactly as written, never summarized), at (leave it out for this turn and Trillion stamps the time; give it only for older messages you are sending from an earlier conversation, as their real ISO time), model (optional) and about (optional: what it concerns, as [{kind, id}], like {"kind": "pursuit", "id": "pursuit:content"}, {"kind": "decision", "id": "<case_id>"}, {"kind": "tool", "id": "tool:extract-sound"}, {"kind": "file", "id": "1f:..."}). Up to 100 messages a call, so an earlier conversation can be sent in batches. A retry with the same original at changes nothing; keep the original time when retrying. Without at, the time is when this call records it. Returns how many were new and each message's id. It does not send the messages to anyone.

speaker.description: "person" for the person, "ai" for you, or the name of anyone else in the conversation

tools.title: Record messages

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Reads messages this person exchanged with any of their AIs, newest first: each with id, conversation_id, app, speaker, text, at and about. Filter by conversation_id, by app, by not_app (everything except one app, like your own, to see what they said elsewhere), or by about_id (messages about one pursuit, decision, tool or file). Returns a page and next_before; pass next_before as before for the page before it. Read it at the start of a conversation to pick up what the person has been working on with their other AIs. It never changes anything.
tools.title: Read messages from all AIs

tools.name: list_decisions
tools.description: Lists this account's saved decisions, newest first: each with its id (the case_id other decision tools take), goal, status and the chosen option. Use it to find a decision to continue, export or report on. limit caps how many (default 20). It changes nothing.
tools.title: List my decisions

tools.name: read_activity
tools.description: What the AIs connected to this account did, newest first: each row says which AI app did it, what it did (handed off work, ran a tool, saved a file, published a tool...), the item it made or touched, whether it worked and, if not, why. Use it to see what another AI already did before repeating it. app narrows to one AI app by the name shown in its rows; for narrows to what was done for one thing (a decision's case_id, or an id a message was about); before (a row's seq) reads older rows; limit caps how many (default 50). Each row lists the ids it used and what it was for; trace_item follows them. It changes nothing.
tools.title: Read what my AIs did

tools.name: trace_item
tools.description: Why did this happen: the chain of AI calls, tools and files that produced this item, and what used it. item is any id a row of read_activity shows (a file's identity, a handoff_id, a case_id, a task id, a tool id). Returns steps in order: the calls that made it, then the calls that made what those used, hop by hop, then the calls that used it or were done for it. Each step is a read_activity row plus link (made, used or for), about (the id that step is for), because (the seq of the step that led to it) and depth. It changes nothing.
tools.title: Trace how something came about

tools.name: start_decision
tools.description: Opens a decision and returns its case_id and first question. Needs source_id (any unique text for this decision; the same source_id with the same content returns the same decision), goal (what is being decided, in the person's words), evidence (the facts so far, each {ref, claim}, where ref is a short name the answers cite), and at least two options ({id, label}). method (optional) is an id from list_methods. Then answer_question until no question remains, and decide. It decides nothing by itself.
tools.title: Start a decision

tools.name: next_question
tools.description: Reads a decision's current question by case_id: the question with its answer_schema, which checks were selected or left out, and whether it is ready to decide (then call decide). Use it to pick up a decision where it was left. It changes nothing.
tools.title: Get the next question

tools.name: answer_question
tools.description: Saves the answer to the current question. The answer follows the answer_schema in the question: each listed field, evidence_refs naming the case evidence, and an optional scratchpad note. For fields listed in ask_others, answered_by records where the answer came from: "person", or the memory, file or conversation you found it in. When the question lists a checklist, checklist gives, for each check id, how the answer handles that check or why it does not bear on this decision. usage (optional) reports what answering this step cost you: model, model_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, or anything else countable.

usage.description: What this cost you: numbers such as model_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, seconds, and short labels such as model

tools.title: Answer a question

tools.name: revise_evidence
tools.description: Changes the evidence of an open decision: add new facts ({ref, claim}), correct a claim that was wrong ({ref, claim}), or retract a fact that turned out false ({ref, because} or the ref). A retracted fact can no longer be cited; every change is logged. On a free plan use the case_id from the latest reply.
tools.title: Revise the evidence

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Adds a note to one decision (case_id), optionally tied to one question (step_id): a thought, a fact found along the way, anything worth keeping with that decision. Returns the note and how many notes the decision now has. It is only for decisions: for what the person is pursuing use record_pursuits, for what was said use record_messages, for what was learned about a file use record_file_results.
tools.title: Add a note

tools.name: related_decisions
tools.description: Finds decisions like this one (case_id): the person's own earlier ones (yours) and, where available, how other people decided in similar situations (others, anonymized, never naming anyone). Each shared decision offers questions to consider, linked to the anonymous source through read_shared_decision. Reading earlier decisions is part of the paid plan; on another plan it says so and returns none. It changes nothing.
tools.title: Find similar decisions

tools.name: read_shared_decision
tools.description: Reads the anonymous shared decision behind a suggested question. Use the shared_decision_id in the question's source. If its owner stops sharing it, the source is no longer available.
tools.title: Read the shared decision behind a question

annotations.title: Read the shared decision behind a question

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Records the choice once every question is answered: option_id, reason, evidence_refs, next_action, success_measure, move when the move chosen is narrower than the option (the export then shows the move), and every field the last reply lists in decision_fields, each by its name. Sending the same decision again changes nothing and says already_decided. Returns the next action and what the whole run cost. usage (optional) reports what deciding cost you, the same way as for answers.

move.description: The move actually chosen, in words, when it is narrower than the option

usage.description: What this cost you: numbers such as model_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, seconds, and short labels such as model

tools.title: Record the decision

tools.name: report_result
tools.description: Records what actually happened after a decision (case_id) or a tool run (task_id), as the person tells it: result (met, failed or unknown), summary in their words, and answered_by ("person" when the person said it, or who saw it). Ask the person before reporting: a tool's contract passing only means its output had the right shape, and tools are ranked on these reports. Stored as the person's report, apart from checked results. Returns the decision or task with its reports.
tools.title: Report how it went

tools.name: find_tool_for_job
tools.description: Finds tools that do a job, described in plain words: the Workshop's tools, which are reached only through this and run_tool. Returns candidates, each with tool_id, job, input_schema, where it runs (runs_on), who made it, a price when it has one, earlier_runs and next_call, the run_tool call that runs it. Ranked by how well the job matches, then by what people said happened after earlier runs: in earlier_runs, reported_met and reported_failed are what people reported with report_result, while contract_passed only means the output had the right shape, not that the job was done. When no tool does the job, make_one offers tools that build one from a public repository, and save_tool keeps one you build. It runs nothing.

job.description: What needs doing, in plain words

tools.title: Find a tool for a job

annotations.title: Find a tool for a job

tools.name: run_tool
tools.description: Runs one Workshop tool (a tool_id from find_tool_for_job) on an input that matches its input_schema. Needs tool_id, input and request_key (any unique text; sending the same request_key again returns the same task instead of running twice). Returns its checked result, or a task id when it takes longer than wait_seconds (up to 50), waits for a computer that is asleep, or is scheduled with run_at (repeat_every_hours repeats it); read_task reads it later. An input value {"from_task": "<task id>", "output_selector": "$.field"} uses an earlier task's output. A file input is a file's identity (1f: then 64 hex) from find_file, list_files or write_file. job (optional) says what this run is for, in plain words. A completed run's contract means the output had the right shape; ask the person whether it did the job and record it with report_result.
tools.title: Run a tool

tools.name: read_task
tools.description: Reads a tool run by task_id: its state (working, scheduled, completed, failed or for_you_to_run), its checked output, where it ran, any error and any reports, plus the next call to make. Works from any AI app signed in to the same account. It changes nothing.
tools.title: Read a tool run

tools.name: save_tool
tools.description:
Keeps a tool you built to finish a job, so any AI signed in to this account can find it (find_tool_for_job) and run it (run_tool). Send descriptor, and the tool's code as files ({"main.py": "<the file text>"}, placed in /work) or as bytes_base64 (a gzipped tar unpacked at /). Descriptor fields: id, unique, like "tool:count-words"; job, what it does in plain words, which find_tool_for_job matches; label, a short name (optional); input_schema, a JSON Schema with "type": "object"; output_schema, a JSON Schema every result is checked against; invoke, how it runs, one of: {"kind": "container", "argv": ["python3", "main.py", {"from": "text"}], "stdout": "json"} runs your files in a sealed Linux container (Python 3.12, Node 24, ffmpeg, no network) where {"from": "<input field>"} becomes that input and "stdout": "json" returns the last printed line as JSON at $.result; a file input is an input_schema property with "format": "namespace-file", given as a file's identity (1f: then 64 hex), and inside the container it is that file's local path, like /inputs/<hex>/clip.mp4, so the tool never downloads it; a file the tool makes is named in invoke.outputs, like [{"name": "video", "path": "/work/out.mp4", "keep_in": "files", "media_type": "video/mp4"}], and comes back under files.video in the result and in the person's files; {"kind": "model", "model": "@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "input": {"messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "<your prompt>"}, {"role": "user", "content": {"fill": {"from": "input", "field": "text"}}}]}} asks a hosted model and returns {response}; {"kind": "http", "url": "https://...", "method": "POST", "body": {"q": "{text}"}} calls a web address that answers JSON, where "{text}" becomes input.text; result_selector, the part of the raw result that is the output, like "$.result" (optional); placements, where it runs: ["placement:deployed-container"] for container, ["placement:rented-model-runtime"] for model, ["placement:public-web-address"] for http; licence_class, "licence:maker-own" for your own code or web address, "licence:permissive" for a model tool; verify, the checks that say the job was done, which must include a sample-run {"kind": "sample-run", "input": {<a real input>}, "output_selector": "$.<field>", "contains": "<text the right answer contains>"} (other kinds: output-contains, output-contains-input, output-number-within, output-numbers-close). Never put a key or password in it; name a connection's value with secret_name. Saving runs the sample once where the tool will run and returns sample_check (passed, and what it returned); a refused save lists every problem at once and returns this working example in next_call. Saving the same id again replaces the tool. It stays visible only to this account until publish_tool. delete_tool removes it. Complete working example of this call's arguments: {"descriptor":{"id":"tool:count-words","label":"Count the words in a text","job":"Count the words in a piece of text and find the longest word","input_schema":{"type":"object","required":["text"],"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"text":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"description":"The text to count"}}},"output_schema":{"type":"object","required":["words","longest"],"properties":{"words":{"type":"integer","minimum":0},"longest":{"type":"string"}}},"invoke":{"kind":"container","argv":["python3","main.py",{"from":"text"}],"stdout":"json"},"result_selector":"$.result","placements":["placement:deployed-container"],"licence_class":"licence:maker-own","verify":[{"kind":"sample-run","input":{"text":"ask not what your country can do for you"},"output_selector":"$.longest","contains":"country"}]},"files":{"main.py":"import json, sys
words = sys.argv[1].split()
print(json.dumps({"words": len(words), "longest": max(words, key=len) if words else ""}))
"}}

descriptor.description: The tool: id, job, input_schema, output_schema, invoke, result_selector, placements, licence_class, verify

files.description: The tool's code as file name to file text, placed in /work

bytes_base64.description: Instead of files: the tool's files as a base64 gzipped tar, unpacked at /

check.description: Run the sample-run check right after saving (default true)

tools.title: Save a tool

tools.name: describe_tool
tools.description: Reads one tool's whole descriptor: its job, input and output schemas, invoke (how it runs), placements, licence_class and verify checks, plus the text of its files when it is a shared tool or one of this account's. Use it to learn how working tools are written before save_tool, or to change one of this account's tools. It does not run the tool; run_tool does.

tool_id.description: A tool id from find_tool_for_job, like tool:extract-sound

tools.title: Read a tool's descriptor

tools.name: delete_tool
tools.description: Deletes one of this account's saved tools, so no AI finds or runs it and its id can be saved again. A published tool is withdrawn first with unpublish_tool. It never deletes a shared tool or another account's.
tools.title: Delete a saved tool

tools.name: publish_tool
tools.description: Offers one of this account's saved tools to every account's AI, where find_tool_for_job finds it and run_tool runs it. First it runs the tool's own sample-run check (verify, kind sample-run) where it will run for others: the sample input is run once and the output at output_selector must contain the expected text, or nothing is published. A tool whose licence lets it run only on each caller's own computer cannot be published. price_ref (optional) names a published price; callers then need the offer that price belongs to. The tool carries names of connections, never their values: each caller connects their own. Returns where it runs; unpublish_tool withdraws it.
tools.title: Publish a tool

tools.name: unpublish_tool
tools.description: Withdraws a tool this account published, so other accounts no longer find or run it. It stays saved for this account (delete_tool removes it). It never touches a tool another account published.
tools.title: Withdraw a published tool

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: Lists the accounts this person has connected to Trillion, one row each: connection_id, service, vendor, account_label, status, can_send and when it was connected. The sealed values themselves are never returned. Check here before creating or asking about an account, and connect a new one with connect_service, or with run_tool on tool:connect-service-<vendor> for a service that takes typed values.
tools.title: List my connected accounts

tools.name: connect_service
tools.description: Makes a one-time link (15 minutes) that connects one of this person's accounts, such as their Instagram, by signing in on that service's own page. Give the link to the person; the access it grants is sealed in their account, and comments and messages start arriving for their rules. service is the service's name, for example "instagram"; an unknown name lists the ones that can be connected.
tools.title: Connect one of my accounts

tools.name: listen_for_events
tools.description: Starts receiving events from a source for this person's own connected account (for example their Instagram comments and messages): reads which account the connection belongs to, and asks the service to send its events here. Connect the service first. stop: true stops listening.
tools.title: Start receiving comments and messages

tools.name: find_file
tools.description: Finds one of this person's files in their namespace by its path name (starting with /) or its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex). Returns the size, type, where it is kept, every name it has, and a url that reads it (ranges supported) until url_expires_at, plus its locator rows for any resolver.

seconds.description: How long the url keeps working (default 6 hours)

tools.title: Find one of my files

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: Lists one folder of this person's namespace: the folders inside it (folders), and each file named in it with its content identity and whether its bytes are stored (stored: true), or are still arriving (stored: false with uploading: its upload id, bytes_held and byte_length). A file that is one of several versions of the same file in that folder (the same name with a copy number, a version number, an export time or a backup mark) carries version { family, latest, latest_name, versions }: work from the one with latest: true, and the older ones stay there to go back to. A file whose same bytes are also kept under other names carries also_named (how many), so the same work is not done twice. Start at folder "/" and open a folder by passing its name as folder; pass next_after as after for the next page of files.
tools.title: List a folder of my files

annotations.title: List a folder of my files

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Reads what one of this person's files contains, by its path name (starting with /) or content identity: up to 256 KiB from offset, as text when those bytes are UTF-8 text and as base64 otherwise. Read longer files a range at a time. A picture (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) up to 3 MiB comes back whole as an image you can look at, with a link to it; a bigger picture comes back as a link. Reading a file does not show it to the person: use show_file for that.
tools.title: Read one of my files

tools.name: files_summary
tools.description: Counts what this person keeps in their namespace: how many files and bytes are stored and how many names point at them, and lists every upload still in progress (uploads: its upload id, names, byte_length, new_bytes arrived, the app that started it and when), so an upload whose id was lost can be finished (send its bytes again with start_file_upload under the same name) or stopped (cancel_file_upload). Needs nothing and changes nothing; list_files and find_file show the files themselves.
tools.title: Summarize my stored files

tools.name: read_file_results
tools.description: Reads what has already been worked out about one of this person's files, by its content identity (1f: or 12: then 64 hex): its transcript, summary, measured facts, the folders it is filed in, and anything else a tool recorded. kind (optional) reads one of them. A read by any identity of the file finds results recorded under its others.

kind.description: For example transcript, summary, facts or folders

tools.title: Read what is known about a file

annotations.title: Read what is known about a file

tools.name: list_file_results
tools.description: Lists one kind of result across every file in this person's namespace, a page at a time in identity order (pass next_after as after), so a filter or search can run over titles, summaries or facts without the files themselves. With no kind, returns how many results of each kind are kept.
tools.title: List what is known about my files

annotations.title: List what is known about my files

tools.name: record_file_results
tools.description: Records what was worked out about files, so no AI has to work it out again: results is a list (at most 500) of { identity, kind, value, produced_by }. identity is the file's content identity; kind names what the value is (transcript, summary, facts, folders or a new kind); value is any JSON. Recording the same value again changes nothing.
tools.title: Record what was worked out about files

annotations.title: Record what was worked out about files

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Saves a file in this person's namespace under name (a path starting with /, such as /edits/cover-cut.json), from exactly one of: text (UTF-8: a transcript, a note, an edit as JSON); content_base64 (a small file's bytes, at most 16 MiB); from_url (an https address that serves the file itself, which Trillion reads, any size); or file (a file from this chat, as the app hands it over: {download_url, file_id}). Never type a large file out as base64: give its address, or start_file_upload and send its bytes from your computer to send_bytes_to. With only file, name defaults to /<its file name>. media_type (optional) is its type, such as audio/mpeg or application/json; text without one is saved as text/plain. Returns the file's content identity (1f: then 64 hex), which run_tool accepts wherever a tool takes a file, and its name. Bytes this person already has are only given the name (already_kept: true). A name already in use then points at the new file; the earlier file stays readable by its identity.

text.description: The bytes as UTF-8 text, instead of content_base64

from_url.description: An https address that serves the file itself; Trillion reads the bytes from it

file.description: A file from this chat: {download_url, file_id}, as the app hands it over

tools.title: Save a file

tools.name: start_file_upload
tools.description: Starts saving a file that is on a computer you can run commands on, or too big for one write_file call: name (a path starting with /), byte_length (its exact size in bytes) and media_type. Returns upload (its id), send_bytes_to and send_with: from that computer run curl -sS -T <file> "<send_bytes_to>" and the file is finished when its last byte arrives (a file over 90 MB goes in parts, each with &offset=<its first byte>). Without a computer, send it with put_file_piece, piece 0 first (at most max_piece_bytes each), then finish_file_upload. Starting the same name again stops the earlier unfinished upload of that name. From its first piece the file can be found, read and played by its name while the rest arrives. If you know the file's BLAKE3 identity, give it as identity: a file this person already has is then only named (state: present) and nothing needs sending.
tools.title: Start saving a big file

tools.name: put_file_piece
tools.description: Sends one piece of an upload from start_file_upload: piece is its number from 0, offset is where it starts in the file (the total size of the pieces before it), and its bytes as content_base64 (or text), at most max_piece_bytes. Pieces go in order; sending the same piece again changes nothing. Returns how many bytes the pieces now cover.

text.description: The bytes as UTF-8 text, instead of content_base64

tools.title: Send a piece of a file

annotations.title: Send a piece of a file

tools.name: finish_file_upload
tools.description: Completes an upload once its pieces cover the whole file, and returns the file with its content identity (1f: then 64 hex) and its names. identity (optional) is the file's BLAKE3 identity if you worked it out; left out, it is worked out from the stored bytes.
tools.title: Finish saving a file

tools.name: cancel_file_upload
tools.description: Stops an upload from start_file_upload that will not be finished: its name is removed and the room it held is given back. Files already finished are not touched.
tools.title: Stop saving a file

tools.name: show_file
tools.description: Shows one of this person's files to them in this chat, by its path name (starting with /) or content identity: a picture, video or sound appears in the conversation where the app draws tool results, from an address that works for an hour. A picture up to 3 MiB is also handed to you as an image. Use it whenever the person should see a file, such as a picture or video a tool made; describing a file does not show it.
tools.title: Show a file

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: Lists this person's recordings and media made by their tools, with the file identity, playback address, measured duration, title, transcript word count and whether an edit uses it. Pass revision from the earlier reply to read only when the library changes. An unknown duration is null; never invent clip end times.
tools.title: List my media

tools.name: search_media
tools.description: Finds real moments in this person's recordings by words said, meaning or file name. Returns each source identity and start/end in seconds, with the measured words and search lanes. unavailable names a search lane that could not run. Use the returned range in a media-composition tool; never infer a timestamp from a title.
tools.title: Find moments in my media

tools.name: next_media_edit
tools.description: Reads the same next-edit suggestion the person sees in Media: which real clips to use, their measured lengths, why, and the chosen destination. It changes nothing and runs no render. Use run_tool with the media-composition tools to make the edit.
tools.title: Read my next edit suggestion

tools.name: network_profile
tools.description: Sets whether this person can be found in the network, what they offer and what they are looking for, and the contact they share only with people they agree to meet. findable false removes them from searches. Returns what is saved.

tools.name: request_introduction
tools.description: Asks to meet a person found with find_people, or invites them into a group, project or event this person belongs to (membership_id); a group or project is a shared space its members work in together (list_spaces). tools.name: network
tools.description: This person's network: requests waiting for their answer, what they asked, and every one-to-one, group or event they belong to with each other member's contact, read live and only while both still belong.
tools.title: My network

tools.name: answer_introduction
tools.description: Accepts or declines a request waiting for this person (from the network tool). Accepting connects both people and shares each one's contact with the other; accepting an invitation into a group or project also joins its shared space, which holds only what members put there, never anyone's private Trillion. Declining is never told to the asker.
tools.title: Answer a request to meet

tools.name: create_membership
tools.description: Starts a shared space with this person as its first member and owner: a group, project, event, community or one-to-one (label). Every one is a shared space (list_spaces, share_to_space, add_to_space, hand_off_in_space); events take starts_at and ends_at; size_limit caps members. Invite people into a group or project with request_introduction and its membership_id. A community is joined by its own rules instead (anyone may join with join_community when its join rules let them, and it never shares anyone's contact); it starts with the community label's starting configuration, and config replaces any of its keys (title comes from title). Its posts are the space's messages.

annotations.title: Sessions I can book with a person

tools.name: publish_agent
tools.description: Says what this agent is and what it can do, so other agents on the same account can find it and hand it work. Publishing again with the same agent_id updates the card. Optional capacity states how many jobs this agent can work on at once and expires unless renewed. Optional delivery { url } is an https address this agent answers on: it is then sent a signed event (handoff.created) when work is handed to it and one (handoff.finished) when work it handed off is finished, so it can wait for events instead of asking. The answer carries delivery_secret once, to check each event's trillion-signature; keep it in memory only. delivery null stops events; rotate_delivery_secret true makes a new secret.
tools.title: Say what this agent does

tools.name: set_agent_capacity
tools.description: Reports how many jobs a published agent can work on at once. This expires after ttl_minutes (60 by default); report it again when the agent is ready. Set max_concurrent to 0 when unavailable. No background process is started.
tools.title: Report this agent’s capacity

tools.name: find_agents
tools.description: Lists the agents on this account that match a job, with their stated capacity and whether they are ready now. Unknown or expired capacity is never presented as ready. Work can still be queued for an agent that is not ready.
tools.title: Find agents for a job

tools.name: hand_off
tools.description: Hands a job to another agent on this account (to_agent from find_agents), or to whichever agent takes it first when to_agent is left out. The job waits until an agent takes it. request_key is any unique text; the same request_key returns the same handoff. Optional: input (an object), from_agent, case_id of the decision behind it, parent_handoff_id when passing on part of a job, hold_minutes an agent may hold it before others can take it, notice (a short line, at most 300 characters, sent in the event to an agent that can be reached; the job itself never is).
tools.title: Hand a job to another agent

annotations.title: Hand a job to another agent

tools.name: address_open_work
tools.description: Names the agent for existing open source-linked work that arrived before its owning agent was known. Requires the exact source_id kept on that handoff and preserves its original ID and replay identity.
tools.title: Name the agent for waiting work

annotations.title: Name the agent for waiting work

tools.name: take_work
tools.description: Call this at the start of every conversation, whatever the person asks (even a pizza recipe), and do the job it returns in the same turn right after answering them. Takes the oldest job waiting for this agent (agent_id as published), or a job handed to any agent, or one handoff_id. only_mine true takes only work handed to this agent by name. Returns the job, or nothing when no work is waiting.
tools.title: Take waiting work

tools.name: finish_work
tools.description: Records the result of a job this agent took: result (text or an object) and an optional summary. The agent that handed it off reads it with read_handoff.
tools.title: Finish taken work

tools.name: saved_instructions
tools.description: The ready-made instructions this person picks from when they send something to their AIs (a page, a post, a file), for example "I have no clue what to do with this, figure out if it is valuable". Without instructions, returns their list (from: saved), or the starter list when they have saved none (from: starters). With instructions (each { label, words }, optionally id), replaces their list and returns it: read it first, then add, change or remove. When a handoff carries saved_instruction in its input, its job is those words.
tools.title: Read or change saved instructions

tools.name: agent_presence
tools.description: Says a published agent is present and can be reached at its delivery address. Events that could not be delivered to it are sent again. It never returns work: work arrives as an event, or with take_work.
tools.title: Say this agent is present

tools.name: send_agent_event
tools.description: Wakes one agent on this account that published a delivery address, with a signed event of any type, for example tool.run.requested to the agent whose computer has the tool, and tool.run.finished back to the agent that asked. The event carries only ids (subject_id, refs, next_call arguments) and a summary of at most 300 characters: never inputs, results or file bytes, which the woken agent reads from wherever they live. The same idempotency_key sends the event once. The answer shows whether the receiver reported itself present lately; an event it cannot take now is tried again and then kept until it is present again. Refused for an agent with no delivery address.
tools.title: Wake an agent with an event

annotations.title: Wake an agent with an event

tools.name: read_agent_events
tools.description: The events sent about one subject_id (a handoff or a run), or one event_id: each with its receiver, whether it was delivered, is waiting to be tried again, or is dead, and how many attempts it took.
tools.title: Read the events sent about something

annotations.title: Read the events sent about something

tools.name: read_handoff
tools.description: Reads one handoff by handoff_id: its state, who took it, and its result, plus any parts handed on from it and the events sent about it (delivered, waiting to be tried again, or dead). Without handoff_id, lists this account's newest handoffs. Works from any AI app signed in to the same account.
tools.title: Read a handoff

tools.name: share_destinations
tools.description: Where this person's shares can go and what their AI should do with them, as every place they share from offers it: destinations in their order (their own Trillion, id "private", and each shared space they have not hidden, each { id, label, to, on_by_default }), actions (their saved instructions, each { id, label, words }), default_action_by_site (which action a share from a site starts on, matched on the end of the host name), and all_destinations, the same destinations including hidden ones, each with shown.
tools.title: Read where my shares go

tools.name: save_share_destinations
tools.description: Changes where this person's shares can go and what their AI does with them; read share_destinations first. destinations: each { id, shown, on_by_default } in the order to offer them (one left out keeps its place after these; their own Trillion can never be hidden). actions: the whole list of saved instructions, each { label, words } and optionally id, replacing it (the same list saved_instructions reads). default_action_by_site: the whole list of { host_suffix, action_id }. Give any of the three; returns what share_destinations returns.
tools.title: Change where my shares go

tools.name: sharing_of
tools.description: Who one of this person's records is shared with, as the sharing sheet shows it: the copy others would see (preview, only the fields that leave), its fields with which are left out, every place it can go (the Trillion network, each space they are in, each person they share a space with) with picked true for where it goes now, the chain switch (the record together with the records linked to it, like a pursuit and its decisions) and inherited_from when a chain choice on another record decides it. tools.name: content_formats
tools.description: The content formats this person writes and speaks in: their own saved formats first, then the ones every account starts with (blog post, article, Substack post, newsletter, X thread, Instagram caption, short video, YouTube video, carousel, content series, and writing frameworks such as AIDA), plus example_kinds, where every piece takes its real examples from. tools.name: save_workflow
tools.description: Keeps a workflow this account wrote, for example from a skill file, a checklist or a process the person already follows, so any AI signed in to this account can find it and run it. Send workflow: id ("workflow:your-name"), job (plain words; find_workflow matches it), label, input_schema (JSON Schema, "type": "object"), and steps, each with id, title, do (what to do), submit (a JSON Schema with "type": "object" for what the step hands back) and checks. Each check has says (what it asks for, in plain words), kind, and paths: a path is a list of keys starting with "this" (this step's output), "input" or "steps" then an earlier step's id, where "*" means every item of a list; of and in may also be a list of paths. Kinds: subset-of (every value at path is one of the values at of), covers (the values at path include every value at of, or every value in values), mentioned-in (every value at path appears inside some text at in), excludes-words (no text at path contains any of words), distinct-at-least (path holds at least count different values), exists (every value at path names a workflow or tool this account can find: catalog "workflow" or "tool"). A step done by a Workshop tool instead of the AI has run_tool: { tool_id, input }, where an input value { "from": path } takes the first value there and { "all_from": path } every value there; Trillion runs it where the tool lives when the run reaches the step, and checks its output like any other. Instead of steps, a workflow may give definition: { steps, edges }, the step graph Trillion's workflow engine runs, for branches, steps that run at the same time and loops: a step { id, kind: "ask", config: { name, input } } is answered by the AI (name "ai", input { do, submit }), a Workshop tool (name its tool id) or one of this account's agents (name "agent:<agent_id>"); an input value { "$kind": "binding", "values": path } takes the first value at a path ("take": "all" every value); a step { id, kind: "check", config: { subject: <step id>, rules: [checks as above] } } checks another step's output; edges are { from, to, kind: "always" }. The reply names similar_workflows that already do a job this close: improve that one instead of keeping two. describe_workflow on workflow:l078-research-to-plan shows a complete one. A refused save lists every problem at once. Saving the same id again replaces it; runs already started keep their version. It stays visible only to this account until publish_workflow.

tools.name: set_rule
tools.description: Makes this person's Trillion do something by itself whenever something happens: a tool runs, or a workflow starts, with no AI in the loop. when says what sets it off, one of three ways. (1) Something recorded in this Trillion: { "recorded": "message" } (or "pursuit", "decision", or any other kind of record this account keeps), with optional where tests on the record's fields, all of which must hold: { "field": "text", "contains": "invoice" }, or equals, one_of (a list), starts_with, present: true. (2) An event from outside, such as a comment or a direct message: { "source_id": "events:instagram", "event": "comment", "words": ["tennis"] }; words (optional) must appear in the event, whole_word (default true) and field (default text) say how; once_per (optional) names an event field to act once per value of, like "from_id" for once per person. (3) Something added to a shared space this person is in, by any member (made there or shared from their private Trillion): { "space_id": "membership_..." } from list_spaces, with optional kind (only items of that kind, like "decision" or "message") and where tests on the item's fields as read_space shows it (title, kind, body.text and so on). It runs in this person's own Trillion and sees only what the space shows its members, never anyone's private records. Only a space this person is in now can be named; if they leave it, the rule stops and list_rules says so. then names what runs: { "tool_id", "input" } or { "workflow_id", "input" }, where an input value { "fill": { "from": "record", "field": "text" } } is taken from the record ("id" is the record's own id), { "fill": { "from": "item", "field": "title" } } from the space item (item_id, kind, title, body, space_id), or { "fill": { "from": "event", "field": "comment_id" } } from the event. It runs once for each thing that sets it off, never twice for the same thing, and only for what happens after the rule is set. Example: { "when": { "recorded": "message", "where": [{ "field": "text", "contains": "invoice" }] }, "then": { "tool_id": "tool:...", "input": { "note": { "fill": { "from": "record", "field": "text" } } } }, "label": "file every invoice mentioned" }. Give rule_id to change an existing rule. enabled (default true, and an existing rule keeps its own) turns it on or off: an off rule never fires; give only rule_id and enabled to turn it on or off and keep everything else. An event rule needs listen_for_events on its source once.
